findings.claim: The only evidence that the 100,000-token input ceiling covers the worst-case request compares a UTF-8 byte count against a token constant and adds a token-denominated framing allowance to it, and the unstated lemma that makes this sound (a byte-level BPE token spans at least one UTF-8 byte) appears in neither the assertion nor the constant's comment, while the exported allowance is consumed by no contract check.
findings.reproduction: Read tests/promptRefinerExecutionContract.test.mjs:78-86: renderedBytes is computed with new TextEncoder().encode(...).length (96,848 bytes) and asserted as renderedBytes + PROMPT_REFINER_MESSAGE_FRAMING_TOKEN_ALLOWANCE <= PROMPT_REFINER_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS, i.e. bytes + tokens <= tokens; then `rg -n "MESSAGE_FRAMING_TOKEN_ALLOWANCE" lib scripts app components` returns only the declaration at lib/promptRefinerExecutionContract.ts:60, so no production path uses it. Adding one sentence to the doc comment stating tokens <= UTF-8 bytes for this tokenizer family would make the bound auditable without changing any number.

findings.claim: The refusal rule still tests `receipt.retryCount !== 0`, which can never be true now that the base schema pins `retryCount: z.literal(0)` at line 131, so that disjunct is unreachable and no test can distinguish its removal.
findings.reproduction: Delete `|| receipt.retryCount !== 0` from lib/promptRefinerReceiptCore.ts:215 and run `node --conditions=react-server --import tsx --test tests/promptRefinerReceiptCore.test.mjs tests/promptRefinerExecutionContract.test.mjs`: it still passes, because any input with retryCount != 0 is rejected by the literal before superRefine runs. Keeping it as defence in depth is a defensible choice; if kept, a one-line comment saying so would stop a later reader from reading it as a live branch.

verdict.nextAction: Merge-ready from this reviewer's side: all five round-0 findings are closed with type-level enforcement rather than prose, the frozen identity and cost figures re-derive from the checked-in catalogue and pricing, and the remaining two items are optional comment-only clean-ups.
